decisions_and_open_items.detail: User selected Gardner’s stricter equipment list. Local guidance uses the 7-foot primary, Gardner backmount BP&W configuration and no steel cylinders with wetsuits. Broader UTD allowances are labeled separately. Individual course standards still apply.

Gardner overview specifies 125 feet; course checklists specify 100 feet; UTD general minimum is 70 feet. The article exposes the local discrepancy and asks the reader to confirm the course packing list; no single new local policy was invented.

decisions_and_open_items.topic: Primary light in Essentials of Rec
decisions_and_open_items.status: Conservative baseline used; checklist reconciliation still needed
decisions_and_open_items.detail: Gardner marks the primary light optional for Essentials of Rec; UTD’s general open-circuit minimum requires primary and backup lights, optional only for OWD. The article recommends primary plus backup for Essentials, rather than asserting a waiver. Confirm the intended local checklist and applicable standard version.

decisions_and_open_items.topic: Shallow Min Deco and travel conventions
decisions_and_open_items.status: User table preserved; source inconsistency retained for review
decisions_and_open_items.detail: The supplied image gives total ascent times of 1, 2 and 2 minutes at 10, 20 and 30 feet. S2 p.5 mentions a minimum three-minute total stop time in its shallow example. S2 pp.2 and 4–6 also express the initial ascent rate as 30 versus 33 ft/min. No universal shallow-stop algorithm or emergency deco schedule was invented. The published table matches S14; profile details require the trained procedure.
S12 describes accidental NDL exceedance and explicitly excludes planned use. Article states that distinction; it does not publish a new emergency-deco calculator or extrapolate the examples.

decisions_and_open_items.status: Illustrative model clarified; no formula/default changes
decisions_and_open_items.detail: Existing default 100-foot model produces 8 minutes, about 40.24 cu ft and 1,600 psi in AL80; source rounds the average to 2.5 ATA and gets 40 cu ft. Other depths are calculated examples, not source-issued UTD reserve tables. Model uses maximum depth, rounded first stop and conservative segment approximations; it is not the recreational NDL/ascent planner.

decisions_and_open_items.topic: Team size: correction to the earlier audit
decisions_and_open_items.detail: S10 PDF p.2, Leader slide, explicitly states Maximum 3 divers on a team. That supports the newer team article. The earlier audit incorrectly described this rule as unsupported. Restored it to the DIR pillar and retained the distinction from course ratios.

decisions_and_open_items.topic: Buoyancy scoring: expanded evidence corrects earlier audit
decisions_and_open_items.detail: Recovered S15 confirms score 2 for >±1 m variation or hands for buoyancy; 3 for <±1 m, 4 for <±0.3 m, 5 for <±0.1 m. Retained the bands and clarified course-specific expectations, which can exceed the v6c general minimum of 3. The earlier unsupported classification reflected an incomplete source set.

decisions_and_open_items.topic: Worksheet emergency breathing rate and unit labels
decisions_and_open_items.status: Source discrepancy documented; conservative existing examples retained
decisions_and_open_items.detail: S16 metric rock-bottom line uses 30 L/min; its imperial example prints .75 cu ft/min and some dimension labels do not match the formulas. S10 explicitly lists emergency stress at 1.0 cu ft/min and 30 L/min as planning values. Kept the site’s existing 1.0 cu ft/min model and did not treat either value as a ceiling if actual team demand is higher. Used dimensional formulas rather than copying inconsistent labels.

UTD alignment is against the supplied v6c, v4.1 and 2020 references, expanded by S15/S16. This is not evidence of later governing UTD revisions. Current GUE entry structure was checked against its official course pages; temperature, historical narrative and owner business facts remain separately attributed context, not UTD standards. No safety outcome or certification is guaranteed.
